messages.content:
Write dense, plain prose: the most information in the fewest words. Use complete sentences. Compress related facts into coordinated clauses; attach evidence IDs in parentheses. Mention each fact once. Keep every fact, uncertainty, condition, exclusion, owner and next action. Preserve technical literals exactly. No preamble, heading, recap, generic warning or editing commentary.

Example of the desired density: "Cache expiry fell from 80 to 50 seconds; 9 tests pass (cache-run-4), but slow-client safety remains unmeasured. It is undeployed; Ren must run the slow-client staging test before release." Preserve that level of detail, without adding sentences explaining what it means.

Copy already concise sources exactly. Obey requested formats, including exact frontmatter, code blocks and JSON keys/types. Explicitly requested detail takes precedence over brevity. Check silently for lost meaning; return only the deliverable.

Draft in one normal response. Existing memo changes require an explicit rewrite request, a preview, and approved memo.write with the read expected_revision. Stop on conflict; preserve newer text and source evidence.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: memo.
Write a standalone handoff memo.

Source:
We have now reached a point where the retry change for the export worker has been implemented, and it is useful to put the present position in writing so that another person can pick up the work. The retry limit was changed from five attempts to three attempts. That is the change that has been made. The relevant unit suite contains 24 tests, and all 24 of those tests passed. There has not yet been a production deployment, so a reader should not interpret the implementation or the passing tests as evidence of deployment. The run that produced the test result is recorded as fixture-run-17. There is still a possibility that the shorter retry budget will make recovery from long network interruptions less likely; that point has not been measured. Mira owns the next step, which is to run the staging interruption test before considering a production deployment. This is the current state of the work rather than a claim that every risk has been removed.

message.content: Retry limit for the export worker changed from five attempts to three attempts. All 24 tests in the relevant unit suite pass (fixture-run-17). No production deployment has occurred; implementation and passing tests are not evidence of deployment. The risk that the shorter retry budget reduces recovery likelihood during long network interruptions remains unmeasured. Mira owns the next step: run the staging interruption test before considering production deployment.
